more.title: New marker panel and free web tool help track stem cells as they develop
more.summary: How can the identity of pluripotent stem cells be determined more reliably during their differentiation? Researchers from the IUF—Leibniz Research Institute for Environmental Medicine and Heinrich Heine University Duesseldorf have systematically validated marker genes for this purpose and developed a web-based application for the automated classification of early cell fates.

more.title: Potatoes could be the secret to better plant-based meat, say food scientists
more.summary: Potatoes could hold the key to making better gluten-free plant-based meat, according to a new study.

more.title: Chaos makes sense of market movements in a crisis
more.summary: Research shows that crises do more than cause financial market volatility and falling share prices—they lead to markets becoming far more interconnected.

more.title: Mechanism behind PARP1-mediated DNA repair characterized, offering insight into targeted cancer therapy
more.summary: When DNA is damaged, cellular processes respond and repair the DNA. Inhibiting DNA damage repair can be therapeutically beneficial in cancers with genetic vulnerabilities related to DNA damage response. Scientists at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital have uncovered a mechanism behind how this process works, which may have implications for cancer treatment. The results were published today in Molecular Cell.

more.title: Malaria Parasite Caught in the Act of Breaking and Entering
more.author: Joanna Thompson
more.summary: To invade red blood cells, the deadly protist creates a temporary molecular portal that disappears behind it — a door we can now see in fine detail. The post Malaria Parasite Caught in the Act of Breaking and Entering first appeared on Quanta Magazine

more.title: Hoarders without borders: Study suggests investors aid international expansion
more.summary: Venture capital firms can help young businesses expand internationally by providing funding as well as market knowledge, expertise and access to professional networks, according to a research literature review published in the International Journal of Management and Enterprise Development.

more.title: Black holes spinning near maximum rate could split in two, calculations suggest
more.summary: Two black holes can collide and merge into one. But could the opposite happen: could a single black hole split into two smaller ones? That question is explored in a new theoretical study: "When Black Holes Admit Pair-of-pants Topologies," published in the journal Physical Review D.

more.title: Paleolithic human DNA reveals east-west connections across Ice Age Europe
more.summary: More than 30,000 years ago, people associated with one of Europe's major Paleolithic cultures (the Gravettian) were more interconnected than previously thought. An international research team led by the University of Vienna has uncovered new genetic evidence of long-distance connections between these populations.

more.title: From sea anemone to human fertility: A new research organism for understanding meiosis
more.summary: Every egg cell and sperm cell depends on meiosis, a tightly choreographed process in which chromosomes find their partners, exchange genetic material and then divide. When meiosis goes awry in humans, the consequences can include infertility, miscarriage and birth defects.

more.title: Surveying the genetic battlefield to uncover the rules of rapid evolution
more.summary: The Malik Lab thrives on competition. But for HHMI investigator Harmit Malik and his team at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, it's the genomes—not the people—that are in conflict. The lab studies rapid evolution—the genetic changes that happen in a species over a few generations rather than thousands of years.

more.title: The permitting deal collides with Trump’s war on offshore wind
more.author: Kathryn Krawczyk
more.summary: This analysis and news roundup come from the Canary Media Weekly newsletter. Sign up to get it every Friday. It’s been years in the making, but the U.S. Senate finally has a bipartisan permitting bill on the table that could speed up the construction of much-needed energy and grid projects. That is, if the Trump…

more.title: Child-led citizen science helps Ecuadorian community tackle beach pollution and shape environmental decisions
more.summary: Pollution from human-generated waste in marine ecosystems has reached critical levels, with cigarette butts (CBs) among the most persistent and harmful pollutants. Globally, an estimated 4.5 trillion cigarette butts are discarded annually, making them the most common type of litter on beaches over the past three decades.

more.title: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial
more.summary: A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment uses personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity, with a clinical trial reporting a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission. Researchers believe the technology could transform PTSD care and pave the way for more precise treatments for other mental health conditions.

more.title: Power cuts and sleep: Students link load shedding to anxiety, disrupted rest and lower grades
more.summary: South Africa endured its worst year of load shedding (scheduled power cuts by the country's utility, Eskom) in 2023. The power went off on 335 of the year's 365 days, often several times a day. Since then, the country has gone more than a year and a half without these planned power cuts.

more.title: Scientists discover a surprising double benefit of exercise for Parkinson’s
more.summary: A seven-year study found that people with Parkinson’s disease who were more physically active experienced slower declines in memory, thinking, and movement abilities. Those exercising more than eight hours per week showed almost no average cognitive decline, suggesting that staying active may offer important benefits as the disease progresses.

more.title: Glowing plants reveal immune responses around infection sites via two colors
more.summary: Researchers at the MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences (LMS) have developed a new way to make glowing biological reporters more accurate, allowing scientists to track gene activity in living plants over days, weeks and potentially even months and years.

more.title: Startups don’t need to go viral to win customers
more.author: Lucas Ropek
more.summary: At TechCrunch Disrupt last week, two founders and a VC discussed how to not just gain an early following but keep one.

more.title: Scientists discover a hidden messaging system deep inside the brain
more.summary: A tiny region deep within the brain has surprised scientists by revealing a remarkably sophisticated communication system. Previously thought to broadcast the same chemical signal throughout the brain, this region actually sends targeted messages that help control learning, attention, and behavior, according to new research in mice.

more.title: As US grid batteries surge, risk of fires plummets
more.author: Julian Spector
more.summary: See more from Canary Media’s ​“Chart of the Week” column . Battery fires are like shark attacks: frightening events that loom cinematically large in the American psyche and almost never actually happen. As batteries have become America’s top choice for new on-demand grid power, community concern about their fire…

more.title: Counting magnetic flux quanta offers new way to measure photon numbers
more.summary: Researchers at AIST have directly observed magnetic flux quanta generated in a superconductor by photon absorption and demonstrated a new principle of photon detection that identifies the number of photons based on the number of these flux quanta.

more.title: Scientists demonstrate AI-designed enzyme for drug synthesis
more.summary: The new RFD4-Proteina unified generative model for protein design—created by the Institute for Protein Design (IPD) in collaboration with NVIDIA—uses advanced AI to generate entirely new protein sequences and structures, achieving computational design success rates five to 10 times higher than previous models and generating candidates five to 10 times faster.

more.title: 'It's pretty toxic… but just a little, I want to be like that': What young men think of manosphere content
more.summary: Masculinity content promises young men self-optimization and success, but often delivers health harms, risk-taking, unattainable standards, gender stereotypes and misogyny. The latter is the strongest predictor of violent extremism.

more.title: VCs, Superhuman Mail founder share red flags about product-market fit
more.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
more.summary: Top investors from Iconiq and Sapphire Ventures, along with Rahul Vohra, the founder of Superhuman Mail, share the do's and don'ts for building hit products.
